chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The black beastly dog, its prey is not eaten, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ordered its killing.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the prey of the black dog considered not edible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi links the impurity of the black dog's prey to a specific prophetic command for its extermination, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the dog's inherent nature (fitrah) renders its catch unfit for consumption. It highlights the distinction between trained hunting dogs and the 'beastly' black dog, emphasizing how prophetic directives on animal elimination directly influence dietary laws (ahkam al-ta'am).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The black dog is the beast, do not eat from its prey because Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered with its killing’.
en.sarwar: 19. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain persons of our people from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from his father from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a people who send their trained dogs to hunt and who mention the name of Allah.

When the dogs go, a stray dog joins them and the dogs jointly hunt. He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not use it for food because you do not know if the trained ones have hunted it or the one without training.’”
